title: Criterion for a surjective affine map to be a regular immersion
statement: Let $T$ and $S$ be commutative rings, let $c>0$, and let $q:T\to S$ be surjective. Suppose $r_1,\ldots,r_c\in\ker q$ form a weakly regular sequence in $T$ (each element is a nonzerodivisor modulo its predecessors). If there is $e\in T$ with $q(e)=1$ and $e\cdot\ker q\subseteq(r_1,\ldots,r_c)$, then $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}T$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is a regular immersion of pure codimension $c$: every point of $\operatorname{Spec}T$ has an affine open neighbourhood whose defining ideal is generated by a weakly regular sequence of length $c$.
